facts.statement: The genus Sinopterus was first described by Wang and Zhou in 2003.
facts.quote: authority: Wang & Zhou, 2003

facts.statement: Fossils of Sinopterus date to the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Sinopterus lived during the Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous in Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Sinopterus (meaning "Chinese wing") is a genus of tapejarid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Sinopterus had a large, toothless, bird-like beak and a long bony crest extending from the front of the skull to a point over the rear.
facts.quote: Sinopterus is known for its proportionally large skull, which has a bird-like pointed beak lacking teeth, and a long bony crest that starts with a tall premaxilla and goes back along the middle of the skull to form a point overhanging the rear of the skull.

facts.statement: Evidence from gut contents suggests that Sinopterus was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Direct dietary evidence based on gut contents suggest that Sinopterus is a herbivore.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Sinopterus dongi had a skull 17 centimeters long and a wingspan of 1.2 meters.
facts.quote: The skull of this individual was 17 centimeters (6.7 inches) long, and the wingspan was estimated to be 1.2 meters (3.9 feet).

facts.statement: Adult Sinopterus could reach a maximum wingspan of 1.9 meters and weigh 2.87 kilograms.
facts.quote: The maximum adult wingspan of this pterosaur would have been 1.9 m, and an individual of this size would have weighed 2.87 kg.

facts.statement: The type species Sinopterus dongi is known from a single specimen described in 2003.
facts.quote: The type species, Sinopterus dongi, is known from one specimen described in 2003.

facts.statement: A second specimen, BPV-077, was described in 2003 as a separate species, Sinopterus gui.
facts.quote: A second specimen, BPV-077, was also described in 2003 by Li, Lü, and Zhang, who classified it in its own species, S. gui.

facts.statement: In 2023, Pêgas and colleagues reviewed the taxonomy of tapejarids and synonymized several Sinopterus species with S. dongi.
facts.quote: In 2023, Rubi V. Pêgas et al. reviewed the recent taxonomic histories of the tapejarids.

facts.statement: Researchers initially suggested Sinopterus was an omnivore, and it was the first tapejarid found outside Brazil.
facts.quote: The authors suggested that it was an omnivore, and noted that it was the first record of a tapejarid outside of Brazil, and the earliest and most complete tapejarid.

facts.statement: Scientists have identified at least one very small juvenile or hatchling specimen of Sinopterus.
facts.quote: At least one very small juvenile (possibly hatchling) specimen has been attributed to Sinopterus.

facts.statement: Studies suggest that juvenile Sinopterus could fly using powered flight rather than just gliding.
facts.quote: They found that while young juveniles would have been excellent gliders, they would not have been reliant on gliding alone as opposed to true flight.

facts.statement: Late juvenile Sinopterus reached sexual maturity at about 79% of adult size before completing skeletal growth.
facts.quote: Osteohistological studies on a late juvenile individual of Sinopterus demonstrates that this taxon achieved sexual maturity before skeletal maturity, with onset of sexual maturity at approximately 79% adult size.

facts.statement: The scarcity of adult fossils compared to juveniles suggests Sinopterus may have been migratory, with adults living in different habitats than younger individuals.
facts.quote: The high number of juvenile Sinopterus fossils found compared to sexually mature adults suggests migratory habits, with mature adults living in different habitats from juvenile and subadult individuals.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether multiple Sinopterus species exist, suggesting many differences are actually growth variations within a single species.
facts.quote: Naish et al. pointed out that all of these features are known to be variable within a single species due to growth, and that there were unlikely to be such a high diversity of extremely similar species in the same ecosystem when their differences are more likely due to variation within a few species.

facts.statement: A 2014 analysis placed Sinopterus species within the clade Tapejaromorpha.
facts.quote: The cladogram below follows the 2014 analysis by Brian Andres and colleagues, showing the placement of two Sinopterus species ("S." gui and S. dongi) within the clade Tapejaromorpha.

facts.statement: Sinopterus is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaurs from the Early Cretaceous found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Sinopterus (en griego "ala china") es un género extinto de pterosaurios pterodactiloideos de la familia Tapejaridae del Cretácico Inferior hallados en la Formación de Jiufotang (Liaoning, China).

facts.statement: The type species S. dongi is based on the holotype IVPP V13363, an articulated and nearly complete skeleton.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, S. dongi, se basa en el holotipo IVPP V13363, un esqueleto articulado y casi completo.

facts.statement: The skull of the type specimen measured 17 centimeters in length, and the wingspan is estimated at 1.2 meters.
facts.quote: El cráneo de este individuo medía 17 centímetros de largo, y la envergadura se estima en 1.2 metros.

facts.statement: It is characterized by a proportionally long skull equipped with a toothless beak resembling that of birds.
facts.quote: Se caracteriza por es cráneo proporcionalmente largo provisto de un pico sin dientes que recuerda al de las aves.

facts.statement: It possessed a long bony crest directed backward and ending in a point.
facts.quote: Tenía una larga cresta ósea dirigida hacia atrás y acabada en punta.

facts.statement: In 2025, researchers reported finding stomach contents within the abdominal cavity of a Sinopterus specimen.
facts.quote: In 2025, the palaeontologist Shunxing Jiang and colleagues reported stomach contents from the abdominal cavity of a Sinopterus specimen.

facts.statement: The stomach contents included gastroliths and phytoliths, marking the first evidence of these items co-occurring in a pterosaur.
facts.quote: These include gastroliths (stones used to aid food processing in the gizzard) and the first evidence of phytoliths in pterosaurs (minerals found in certain plants which persist after their decomposition), and the first evidence of these co-occurring in a pterosaur.

facts.statement: Phytoliths identified as belonging to the Poaceae family, gymnosperms, or ferns indicate that Sinopterus had a diverse diet of plants.
facts.quote: Some of the phytoliths of the specimen were identified as the angiosperm family Poaceae as well as gymnosperms or ferns, indicating Sinopterus had a diverse diet of plants.

facts.statement: Bite force estimations and skull similarities suggest Sinopterus had a herbivorous diet of fruits, seeds, and resistant plant matter.
facts.quote: They also stated that bite force estimations of Tapejara had suggested a herbivorous diet of fruits, seeds, and more resistant plant matter, and added that the similarity between their skulls indicated similar bite forces, supporting a herbivorous diet for both.

facts.statement: A second species, S. gui, was named by Li, Lü, and Zhang in 2003 based on specimen BPV-077 from the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, S. gui, fue nombrado por Li, Lü y Zhang en 2003 basado en BPV-077, otro esqueleto de la Formación Jiufotang.

facts.statement: S. gui differs from S. dongi mainly by its smaller size and the presence of a notarium, though this distinction is controversial.
facts.quote: Este difiere de S. dongi mayormente por su tamaño emnor (solo la mitad del tamaño de S. dongi) y la presencia de un notarium, aunque esto se ha controvertido.

facts.statement: Many subsequent studies have found that S. gui simply represents a younger specimen of S. dongi.
facts.quote: Muchos estudios posteriores han encontrado que S. gui simplemente represneta un espécimen más joven de S. dongi.

facts.statement: A third species, S. jii, was referred to Sinopterus in 2007.
facts.quote: Una tercera especie fue referida a Sinopterus en 2007, S. jii.

facts.statement: Studies published in 2007 and 2011 showed that H. jii was more closely related to Sinopterus than to the other two species assigned to Huaxiapterus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, dos estudios posteriores publicados en 2007 y 2011 mostraron que H. jii estaba en realidad más cercanamente relacionado con Sinopterus que a las dos otras especies asignadas a Huaxiapterus, "H." corollatus y "H." benxiensis.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that Huaxiapterus jii should be reclassified as Sinopterus jii and that the other two Huaxiapterus species require new genus names.
facts.quote: Ambos grupos de investigadores concluyeron que Huaxiapterus jii debería en consecuencia ser reclasificado como Sinopterus jii, y que las dos otras especies de "Huaxiapterus" requieren un nuevo nombre de género.

facts.statement: Sinopterus lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Sinopterus is the family Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tapejaridae

facts.statement: Sinopterus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

rejected.statement: The smallest known Sinopterus specimen has a wingspan of slightly under 25 centimeters.
rejected.quote: It has a wingspan of slightly under 25 centimeters (10 in), making it smaller than all but a few specimens of hatchling pterosaurs.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'has a wingspan of slightly under 25 centimeters'

rejected.statement: Researchers concluded the gut contents confirmed herbivory and excluded a generalist diet because no undigested bones, scales, or insect exoskeletons were found.
rejected.quote: These researchers considered the gut contents confirmation of herbivory, and excluded a generalist diet for Sinopterus as for example no undigested bones, scales, or insect exoskeletons were found.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'no undigested bones scales or insect exoskeletons were'
